The November edition · Season 2 · No. 5

Georgia, all the way down

November belonged to one club. Georgia played eight league games, lost none, scored thirty-five and conceded four, and went from thirteenth in the table — with games in hand — to first. They have the Player of the Month, the month’s top scorer, its two assist leaders and five of the Team of the Month, and they finished it with Sergiño Dest at the World Cup.

By the Touchline desk · read from the save on Friday, December 2, 2022

What this edition is. Back on the Academy beat after two World Cup specials: all sixty league results from November, the table and a November-only table, the power rankings, the Player and Team of the Month, every one of the 352 players graded by role, the development desk, the Youth League draw, the Under-20s’ championship, the 2023 mock draft, the Class of 2022 in the Premier — and the Garrett file, which now comes with pictures.

The month in one line. Georgia took twenty points from twenty-four and are the only unbeaten club left. North Carolina are a point behind them. Michigan, who were our number one, lost to Oklahoma on November 9 and won their other four. UCLA, the champions, took one point from six games and are sixteenth of the Sixteen.

November in the league

Every Academy result from the month

Sixty league matches, 302 goals — five a game, which says more about the bottom six than the top sixteen. Gold-edged tiles are meetings between two of the Sixteen; the rest are the Sixteen against the six schools outside it.

35–4 Georgia

Eight games, no defeats

Six wins and two draws — 1–1 at UCLA and 1–1 at Texas on the last night of the month — and a 4–1 win over Washington, who were top when November started. Georgia have now gone sixteen league games unbeaten, and Sergiño Dest missed the last three at the World Cup.

26–3 Florida State

The meanest month

Four wins and a draw, three goals conceded in five, 3–1 over Washington and 8–0 at Oregon. Florida State were fifteenth on September 30. They are sixth, level on points with fifth.

5–1 Michigan

The best win

Michigan beat North Carolina 5–1 on November 26, the only defeat the Tar Heels took all month. Michigan also beat Alabama 4–3 in Ann Arbor with a guest in the stands.

13–0 Oklahoma

The biggest win

Oklahoma beat Oregon 13–0 on November 19. Alejandro Pineda scored three; Malik Tillman, Jackson Conway and Julian Araujo two each. Oregon have conceded 113 in seventeen league games.

1point UCLA

The champions, sixteenth

Five defeats and a draw — against Georgia, of all teams. UCLA conceded twenty-nine goals in six league games and are sixteenth of the Sixteen, with Paxton Pomykal still grading 85.2.

1win TCU

Twelve and none, then one

TCU beat Louisville 2–1 on November 19 with a 94th-minute winner from Amir Richardson. It is their first league win of the season. They are twentieth.

Power rankings

Points rate, goal difference, November form, the grades and squad ability · movement since Oct 31

The model now weighs points per game (30%), goal difference per game (20%), November points per game (20%), the average ability of each club’s best eleven (15%) and the average Touchline Grade of the same eleven (15%). The new form term is there because two months of a season should count for more than one.

Georgia Bulldogs

11–5–0 · 38 pts · +53 · 1st in the table · November 20 pts · top-11 ability 120.7 · top-11 grade 78.7

Up one, to first. Georgia are top of the table, unbeaten in sixteen, and had the best November in the league by every measure we keep: twenty points, thirty-five scored, four conceded. Juan Pablo Torres is at the top of the grades on 99.0 with twenty-seven assists; Ronaldo Damus is the Player of the Month. The question left is whether anybody can take a point off them that is not a draw.

Player of the month

November 1–30 · all competitions
Georgia · Advanced Forward · 23 years old

Ronaldo Damus

6Goals
3Assists
9Matches
8.57Avg rating
404Minutes

Nine appearances, four of them starts, 404 minutes — and nine goal involvements, one every forty-five minutes. Damus had the best average rating of anyone in the league in November (8.57), a hat-trick against Louisville on November 5, and the opener after two minutes against Akron. He is joint second in the league’s scoring race with twenty-six, level with Jonathan David and six behind Iloski.

The case against him is that he did not play much, and that is also the case for Georgia: their head coach rotated through the busiest month of the season and lost nothing. Juan Pablo Torres (seven assists, 8.53) and Matías Pellegrini (seven assists, 8.27) would have been fine winners. Alex Mighten scored more goals than anybody, seven. We went with the player who turned the fewest minutes into the most goals.

His grade has gone from 83.9 to 90.3, ninth in the league. He is twenty-three, graduates in June, and is thirteenth on our 2023 board.

Touchline Grades

Month three · every player scored against his own position

The grade measures what a player did, never what the game says he is: every one of the 352 players is scored against the others doing his exact job, on the numbers that job is for, with average rating capped at a quarter of the weight and small samples pulled toward the middle. Sixty-one is average; the eighties are All-League; ninety and above is the best in the league.

Month three. The qualifying line moves from 600 to 700 minutes; the shrinkage constant stays at 350. Every player in the Sixteen is over the line. Movement is against the published October 31 grades.

The Garrett file, No. 4

Rumblings · a recurring item

He went. He talked. Now you can watch.

Daniel Garrett was in Ann Arbor on Saturday, November 12. He sat in the main stand with his father for Michigan 4, Alabama 3 — the first thing in this file we printed before it happened and then saw happen. He stayed for all ninety minutes, and he was still there when Alabama’s Erik Dueñas, a nineteen-year-old inverted wing back, scored their third on 79 minutes to set up the last ten.

Afterwards he spoke to Touchline for about four minutes, on the concourse, with his father next to him. He is fourteen; we kept it short and we kept it to football.

“I watch the wing backs. That’s what I do at every game. Where they stand when we’ve got the ball, whether they come inside. Tonight both teams’ full-backs were basically midfielders, and that’s how I want to play.”
“Michigan’s the closest to home. That doesn’t mean anything yet. I just like coming here.”

Asked whether anybody had made him an offer, he looked at his father, and his father said they were not talking about that. That is the answer we expected and the right one.

Touchline Live. Since November 19 this desk has been streaming Garrett’s under-15 matches for Livonia Metro, his academy side, with a fixed camera behind the dugout and one commentator. Three games so far. What they show is a left-footed player who can play on either side, who steps into central midfield when his team has the ball and is back in the line when it does not — the inverted wing back’s job exactly. It is under-15 football, on a public park, against other fourteen-year-olds. It is also the first time anyone outside a scouting department has been able to judge him with their own eyes.

And the panel has. Every one of them, separately, used some version of the same word.

The whispers. Two new names this month, and we are printing them as whispers because that is what they are. People around Texas have asked about him. People around UCLA have asked about him. Neither club has said anything to us on the record, nobody has given us a timeline, and nobody has told us there is an offer. What we can say is why each would want him: Texas lose Matthew Real, their left-sided wing back, in June; UCLA are sixteenth and their best wing back, Bryan Reynolds, grades 70.2.

The frame is unchanged. An American fourteen-year-old arriving with this much noise has a poor base rate, and the one everybody remembers from 2004 did not become what he was supposed to. We have watched three games on our own stream now. That is three more than last month, and it is still three.

What we cannot

  • Whether Texas or UCLA are formally recruiting him. Both have asked about him. Asking is not recruiting.
  • Whether there is an offer. From anyone. His father would not discuss it.
  • Whether Ann Arbor was a recruiting visit. Michigan still will not say either way.
  • Whether Alabama noticed. Their head coach flew to Qatar eleven days later.
  • A timeline. Nobody has given one, and nobody has promised anything.

The wing-back math, from the save

  • Michigan lose Bret Halsey (82.0), the third-best wing back in the league, in June.
  • Texas lose Matthew Real (74.1), the left-sider; Jonathan Gómez (74.0) stays.
  • UCLA lose nobody at wing back and have nobody above 70.2 there.
  • Only three wing backs in the league grade above 80: Booth, López and Halsey. Two graduate.

The tie of the round

Miami v Paris Saint-Germain

Miami drew the biggest name in the pot. They are eleventh in the Academy and in the form of their season — four straight league wins to end November — with two of the league’s top ten graded players, Jonathan Perez and Josh O’Brien.

The strange one

UCLA v Corinthians

UCLA are sixteenth in the Academy and took one point in November. In Europe they have the competition’s best creator and the keeper with the most clean sheets. Corinthians’ under-20s will be the first team this season to find out which UCLA turns up.

Seven games, fifty-one goals, none against

North American U20 Championship · the U.S.A. are champions

The Under-20s won the regional championship on November 16, beating Mexico 4–0 in the final. Ricardo Pepi scored three of the four, in the 29th, 53rd and 90th minutes; Caden Clark scored the first after four. It was their seventh win in seven, and they did not concede a goal in any of them.

The run. After the group — thirteen past Barbados, six past the Cayman Islands, ten past Guyana, five past Honduras — the knockout rounds were closer only by comparison: 8–0 against Haiti (a Pepi hat-trick, two for Brian Gutiérrez), 5–0 against Jamaica (a Cade Cowell hat-trick), 4–0 against Mexico.

What it means. Eighteen of the twenty players are in the Academy, and most of them will be back in it by the weekend. It is the third regional title in a row for the United States. Pepi and Cowell are now on this desk’s 2026 World Cup board; Słonina, who kept seven clean sheets, is in our twenty-three.

Still none from USC. The USC head coach picks this squad. He won the tournament without any of his own players, again.

The World Cup, briefly

The full story is in World Cup Special No. 2

The U.S.A. went out in the group on Thursday night: 4–0 against Egypt, 2–2 with Norway after leading 2–0, and 3–1 against Belgium after leading on 79 minutes. Eleven of the twenty-three were Academy players. Konrad De la Fuente (Washington) scored four, one off the Golden Boot lead; Daryl Dike (Florida) scored the goal that briefly put them top of the group.

What it did to the Academy: Georgia played three league games without Sergiño Dest and won two of them; Washington lost at Georgia and beat UCLA without Busio and De la Fuente; Texas were without Josh Sargent for their last three.

The panel

Touchline’s fictional pundits on the month
DR
Dale Rourke
Rourke Unfiltered
I watched the Garrett stream. Three games. I want it on the record that I said “incredible upside” before anyone else on this panel, and I want it equally on the record that it was under-fifteens on a park and I have been fooled before.
NO
Nadia Okafor
The Whiteboard
Watch where he stands when his side has the ball. Not the tackles, not the touches — the starting position. He is already inside the full-back line doing a job most college wing backs learn at nineteen. Incredible upside, and I do not say that about fourteen-year-olds.
TB
Theo Brandt
The Ledger
Georgia: thirty-five scored, four conceded, unbeaten in sixteen, and the fewest minutes of any Player of the Month we have had. That is not a hot streak, that is a squad. As for the Garrett boy: incredible upside, zero data. I will grade him when there is something to grade.
WK
Walt Kearney
Kearney’s Corner
Texas and UCLA asking about a kid from Livonia is the most interesting thing that has happened to Michigan all season, and Michigan beat North Carolina five–one. If I were in Ann Arbor, I would stop being coy about whether that was a recruiting visit.
HB
Hal Brannigan
The Brannigan Board
Incredible upside. There, I have said it, and it is on the board in pencil, which is the only way I write fourteen-year-olds. Circle the name. Do not ink it.
JO
Jess Ocampo
Touchline Live
I called all three of his games from behind the dugout. He never once stood where the other left back stood. He is going to be asked about a lot of things this year; he should be asked about that first.

Touchline is fiction. It’s an in-universe sports desk for a Football Manager 2022 save. The tables, results, every appearance, goal, assist, rating and ability figure on this page were read from the save on December 2, 2022. Player statistics are all competitions unless a line says league. Head coaches are referred to by role only. Real players appear only through their on-pitch record in the save. Club crests are Touchline’s own designs in each school’s colours, not official marks.

Touchline Grades, the power rankings, the Team of the Month, the 2023 board and the mock draft are this desk’s own models, not figures the game produces. The mock uses today’s USLP table as a stand-in for a draft lottery that has not been run.

Daniel Garrett is a fiction inside a fiction. He does not yet exist in the save, and neither do his father, Livonia Metro, Touchline Live, or the people around Texas and UCLA who have asked about him. The Garrett file is a storyline this desk is building in the open, and it will be labelled as such every time it appears until the day he signs somewhere and starts producing numbers like everybody else.

All quotes are invented for this fictional universe. Quotes come only from Touchline’s fictional panel and from Daniel Garrett, who is fictional. No real person is quoted.
